_provenance.why: These 15 blocks are the lesson-page inventory that ships in the Unit 1 printed exercises a teacher already holds. They were repaired in theme PR #110 and #111 and pass that repo's validateVoice, so importing them keeps the guide and the exercise saying the same thing about the same page rather than drifting.
_provenance.changed_on_import: the phrase "out loud" removed in 7 places, the one staging idiom the theme pass left behind

1.1.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.1) has the Hello, AP CSA editor exercise and a six-item Tier 2 practice set. The editor exercise is built to be broken: a deleted semicolon and a misspelled println both stop the compiler, and the two messages read differently.
activities: Run the 1.1 Java editor exercise as written and confirm the expected output.
Break it: remove the semicolon, run, and read the compiler message.
Break it differently: misspell println as printn, run it, and compare the compiler message to the missing-semicolon one.
Complete the Tier 2 practice questions, six items, with the error-bucket vocabulary open.

1.2.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.2) has the Java editor exercise for declarations, a six-item Tier 2 practice set covering type categories, the three primitives in scope, declaration syntax and the exclusions, and the Tier 3 Library Checkout System challenge.
activities: Run the 1.2 Java editor exercise: declare one int, one double, and one boolean, print all three, and confirm the expected output.
Break it on purpose: change the int declaration to hold 2.5, run it, and read the compiler's type mismatch message.
Complete the six Tier 2 practice questions. For every wrong choice containing long, float, short, byte or char, write 'out of scope' next to it.
Tier 3 Library Checkout System: of double bookId = 4271.0; int lateFee = 2.50; boolean isCheckedOut = "true"; work out which compile, which do not, and which compiles with the wrong type.
Play one game round, Variables Bug Hunt or Java Wordle: Variables, as the last five minutes.

1.3.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.3) has the Java editor exercise, eight Tier 2 AP practice items, and the Tier 3 School Store Vending Machine challenge. The eight items cover print and println layout, expression types, integer division with remainder, escape sequences in a Windows path, compound precedence, ArithmeticException segments, the average-precedence trap, and newline counting.
activities: Run the 1.3 editor exercise, then modify it: change one operand from 2 to 2.0 and describe in one sentence what changed about the output and why.
Tier 2 output trace: for the segment println("Status: "), print("OK"), println(), print("Done"), write the output before revealing. The answer is Status: on line 1, OK on line 2, Done on line 3.
Tier 2 division set: work the 250 / 8 and 250 % 8 item (answers 31 and 2) and the 14 / 4 versus 14.0 / 4 versus 14 / 4 * 2 typing item (only the first and third are int).

Tier 3 School Store Vending Machine, Part A: trace changeCents = 100 - 65, quarters = changeCents / 25, remainder = changeCents % 25 and predict the output. The answers are 1 quarter and 10 leftover cents.
Tier 3 Part C on paper: explain why "Change: $" + changeCents / 100 prints Change: $0 when changeCents is 35, and rewrite it using 100.0 so it prints Change: $0.35.
Play one round of the Output Predictor game or the Expressions Bug Hunt as the closer.

1.4.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.4) has the Java editor exercise, eight Tier 2 AP practice items, and the Tier 3 Science Fair Score Tracker. The items cover assignment tracing, null with primitives, uninitialized locals, widening and narrowing, integer division stored into a double, the broken swap, valid assignment sets, and the Scanner-context item.
activities: Run the 1.4 editor exercise, then edit it: comment out the initialization of one variable, run it, and read the compiler's 'might not have been initialized' message aloud.
Tier 2 trace: int val = 4; val = val * 3; val = val - 5; val = val + val; predict the printed value (answer 14), then check with the editor.
Tier 2 compile-or-not set: decide which of String label = null; int count = null; double ratio = null; compile. Only the String line does.
Tier 2 assignment validity: for int x = 6; double y = 2.5; boolean flag = true; decide which of y = x; x = y; flag = (x > 4); compile. The first and third do.
Tier 3 Science Fair Score Tracker Part A: trace score and bonus through all four assignments with an entered value of 50 and predict the output. The answer is 80.
Tier 3 Part C on paper: rewrite the three assignment statements so bonus doubles before the first addition, then state the new printed result, which is 90.
Play one round of the Assignment Tracing Output Predictor or the Assignment Statements Bug Hunt as the closer.

1.5.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.5) has the Java Code Editor exercise, where a real compiler truncates in front of the student, the Tier 2 AP Practice set, and the Tier 3 Mastery Challenge, The Track Team Timer, which puts truncation and round-off error in one problem.
activities: In the Java Code Editor, print (double) 7 / 2 and (double)(7 / 2) in the same program and confirm the outputs are 3.5 and 3.0.
In the same editor, set an int to Integer.MAX_VALUE, add 1, and print it. The wrapped value is the point.
Print 0.1 + 0.2 and have every student copy the exact printed value into their notes, all digits.
Complete the Tier 2 practice questions, writing the value of every sub-expression before selecting an answer. Nothing in this set is meant to be answered from a guess.
Play one of the two games, Output Predictor or Bug Hunt.

Work Parts A and B of the Tier 3 Mastery Challenge, The Track Team Timer, together. Part A produces 12.6 rather than the expected 12.7, and the reason is round-off error; Part B is fixed by adding 0.5 before the cast.

1.6.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.6) has the Java Code Editor, which verifies traces already written on paper, the Tier 2 AP Practice set, and the Tier 3 Mastery Challenge on the shelf-count sequence.
activities: Before touching the editor, each student writes a paper trace of int n = 100; n /= 4; n %= 7; n += n; and predicts the final value. It is 8.
Type the same sequence into the Java Code Editor with a println after each statement and confirm the printed values 25, 4, 8 against the paper trace.
In the editor, run double total = 9.0; total /= 2; and confirm it prints 4.5, then change the declared type to int and observe what happens to the same statement.
Complete the Tier 2 practice questions, writing the value after every line before selecting an answer.
Play the game on the lesson page. It runs one trace at a time.

Work Parts A and B of the Tier 3 Mastery Challenge together. Part A traces the shelf sequence to 0, and Part B asks which single statement is equivalent to shelf += shelf; the answer is shelf *= 2 because it doubles for any value, while a hardcoded number only works for one.

1.7.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.7) has the Tier 2 AP Practice set, which walks through class descriptions for Student and Car and asks for each member to be classified, and the Tier 3 Mastery Challenge, The Library Card System.
activities: Read one Math documentation line and answer the three questions it raises: what it needs, what it gives back, what it promises.
In the Java Code Editor, call Math.sqrt, Math.abs, and Math.pow once each and record the exact printed output, noting which results print with a decimal part and why.
Complete the Tier 2 practice questions. Each classification item turns on one word in the description, such as stores, tracks, can or returns; name that word.
Work Part A of the Tier 3 Mastery Challenge, The Library Card System: sort cardholderName, booksCheckedOut, expirationYear, checkOut, returnBook, and isExpired into attributes and behaviors.

Work Part B together: given the documentation line void checkOut(String title), state what the method needs (one String), what it returns (nothing, because the return type is void), and write a sample call.
Part C asks why it is safe and efficient to use a class without reading its implementation.

1.8.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.8) has the Tier 2 practice questions and the Tier 3 Mastery Challenge, The Grade Calculator. This is the one Unit 1 lesson with no Java editor exercise, so all of it is reading and reasoning.
activities: Tier 2 question 1 (the commented-out score line) on a show-of-hands vote before anyone speaks, then one student explains the answer 20.

Tier 2 questions on the index precondition, the largest-element postcondition, and the setTemperature(90) scenario. For each, name which answer choice describes the method checking something, and eliminate it on that basis alone.

Tier 3 Part A and Part B: fill in the precondition and the postcondition for letterGrade(int score) given that the method handles 90-100 as A, 80-89 as B, and so on, and does not handle values outside 0-100.

Tier 3 Part C in writing: a classmate calls safeDivide(10, 0) on a method with precondition b != 0. Three to five sentences on what the precondition means, whether the method must handle the call safely, and what the caller should have done.

1.9.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.9) has the Java editor exercises, where call-by-value fails on a real compiler rather than on paper, the Tier 2 practice set, and the Tier 3 Mastery Challenge, The Temperature Converter.
activities: In the 1.9 Java editor: write a void method that doubles its int parameter, call it on a variable set to 7, print the variable, and confirm 7 prints. Then rewrite it as a value-returning method and assign the result so 14 prints.
Tier 2 signature question: identify the signature of public double computeTax(double income, int dependents) and say which distractor added the return type.
Tier 2 trace question: predict the output of the triple(4) segment (A, B, 12 order) before running it, then run it.
Tier 2 overload question: given process(int x), process(double x), and process(int x, int y), decide whether the class compiles and justify with signatures.
Tier 2 argument-matching question: for signature scale(double factor, int count), decide which of scale(2.0, 3), scale(2, 3), and scale(3, 2.0) fail to compile, and why.
Tier 3 The Temperature Converter, Parts A and B: which overload runs for toCelsius(98.6), and which runs for toCelsius(100.0, "F") after a two-parameter version is added.

1.10.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.10) has the Java editor exercises, the Tier 2 practice set, two games, and the Tier 3 Mastery Challenge, The Game Randomizer.
activities: In the 1.10 Java editor: print Math.abs(-8), Math.sqrt(16.0), and Math.pow(2, 8), predicting all three outputs on paper first, then confirming 8, 4.0, and 256.0.
Break it on purpose: delete Math. from one of those lines, run it, and read the compiler message. Restore it, then try int x = Math.sqrt(16.0); and read that message too.
Tier 2 questions: the value of Math.pow(2, 8), which expression gives a random int from 10 to 20 inclusive, and which value Math.random() can never return.
Tier 2 static-method questions: which of Math.pow(3.0, 2.0), new Math().sqrt(9.0), and Math.abs(-100) are valid calls, and why the middle one is not.
Choose one game: Output Predictor (predict the exact value printed or stored, six items) or Bug Hunt (find the one buggy line in each snippet, seven items).
Tier 3 The Game Randomizer, Parts A and B: the possible range of (int)(Math.random() * 100), and the value of Math.pow(2, score1 % 5) when score1 is 7.

1.11.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.11) has the Java editor exercise, an eight-question Tier 2 AP Practice set that leans on the four-method return-type table, two games, and the Tier 3 Mastery Challenge, The Geometry Calculator.
activities: Run the 1.11 Java editor exercise as written and confirm the expected output before changing anything.
Modify the editor exercise: replace Math.pow(2, 8) with Math.pow(8, 2) and read the new output to prove argument order matters.
Work the eight Tier 2 practice questions. For each random-range item, write the minimum and maximum substitutions in the margin before choosing.
Choose one game: Output Predictor (six questions, type the exact output including any decimal point) or Bug Hunt (seven snippets, one buggy line each).
Finish with Tier 3, The Geometry Calculator, Parts A, B, and C. Part C asks for the perimeter line and an explanation of why the result is a double.

1.12.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.12) has the Java editor exercise, a six-question Tier 2 AP Practice set that leans on the memory diagram from the notes, one game, and the Tier 3 Mastery Challenge, The Library System.
activities: Run the 1.12 Java editor exercise as written and confirm the expected output.
Modify it: add a second reference variable that is assigned from the first, reassign the first, then print both, and check the result against your prediction before running.
Work the six Tier 2 practice questions. For every question involving two variables, draw the boxes and the addresses before choosing an answer.
Choose one game: Output Predictor for Objects and References (six questions) or Bug Hunt (seven snippets, one buggy line each).
Finish with Tier 3, The Library System, Parts A, B, and C. Part C is a four-point written response on class versus object using the Book class, so draft it in complete sentences.

1.13.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.13) has the Java editor exercise, an eight-question Tier 2 AP Practice set built on the four-part creation pattern, one game, and the Tier 3 Mastery Challenge, The Bank Account.
activities: Run the 1.13 Java editor exercise as written and confirm the expected output.
Break it on purpose: delete the keyword new from a creation line, run it, and read the compiler message. Then restore it.
Break it a second way: pass a double literal to a constructor whose parameter is an int, run it, and compare that message with the previous one.
Work the eight Tier 2 practice questions. For every question with overloaded constructors, write the matching signature in the margin before choosing.

Choose one game: Output Predictor for Object Creation (six questions, with the class definitions available behind the View class definition control) or Bug Hunt for Instantiation (seven snippets, one buggy line each).

Finish with Tier 3, The Bank Account, Parts A, B, and C. Part C asks for a third overloaded no-arg constructor plus an explanation of why three constructors may share one name, so write it in complete sentences.

1.14.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.14) has the Java Code Editor exercise, the Tier 2 practice set, two games, and the Tier 3 Mastery Challenge, The Temperature Sensor.
activities: Run the 1.14 Java editor exercise as written and confirm the expected output before changing anything.
Break it on purpose twice: remove the parentheses from one call (read the compiler message aloud), then assign a void call to an int variable and compare the two messages.
Complete the eight Tier 2 practice questions, naming for each call whether it is void or value-returning before choosing.
Play either Output Predictor or Bug Hunt for instance methods; require a written prediction before each reveal.
Tier 3 Mastery Challenge, The Temperature Sensor: Parts A and B are a trace with a reading column, and Part C is the aliasing explanation, scored against a 4-point rubric.

1.15.intro: The live lesson page (Unit 1 Link Sheet, row 1.15) has the Java Code Editor exercise, eight Tier 2 practice questions, a game, and the Tier 3 Mastery Challenge, The Username Generator, which closes the unit.
activities: Run the 1.15 Java editor exercise as written and confirm the expected output before editing anything.
Modify it twice: call a substring without storing the result and print the original (immutability), then reassign and print again, so both behaviors appear side by side in one run.
Complete the Tier 2 practice set, writing the numbered index line under every String before choosing an answer.
Play Output Predictor or Bug Hunt for String methods; require a written prediction before each reveal and log every miss by trap name.

Tier 3 Mastery Challenge, The Username Generator: Parts A and B are a trace, and Part C is scored against a 4-point immutability rubric. toLowerCase appears in the problem but is not on the AP Quick Reference, so treat it as given; the tested pieces are substring, indexOf and immutability.
